description: Discover natural synchronization points within a DEFLATE stream where the decoder state can be unambiguously reconstructed, enabling safe parallel entry. Uses information-theoretic analysis of the compressed bitstream to identify positions where entropy temporarily drops, indicating block boundaries or highly predictable state.
mathematical_formalization: Define local entropy H_w(p) = -sum over window w of p(x)*log(p(x)) at position p. Sync points S = {p : H_w(p) < tau} where tau is a threshold. At sync points, decoder state is (nearly) deterministic. Probability of valid sync point at random position ~ 2^(-k) where k = bits of decoder state. For DEFLATE with 32KB window and 15-bit codes, effective k ~ 15-20 bits.
analogical_connections: Frame synchronization in digital communications: finding sync words in continuous streams
Paragraph detection in NLP: finding natural break points in continuous text
pugz's technique: scanning for valid DEFLATE block headers in compressed genomic data
implementation_hypothesis: Scan the compressed bitstream in parallel (SIMD) for candidate sync patterns: DEFLATE block headers (BFINAL=0/1, BTYPE=01 or 10), followed by plausible Huffman table descriptors. Score candidates using a Bayesian classifier trained on real DEFLATE streams. Use SIMD byte-scan (pcmpistri on x86) to find candidates at ~16 bytes/cycle. Feed high-scoring candidates to speculative decoders.
experiment_seed: Analyze 10,000 real DEFLATE streams to characterize the statistical properties of block boundaries. Implement SIMD-accelerated sync point scanner. Measure false positive rate and discovery latency vs brute-force trial decompression (as in rapidgzip).
